title: Ribbon-Cutting Ceremony
subtitle: The crowd waited, then it began with a single spark.

trails.title: The Foundation's Note Slips
trails.description: Everyone could use a few slips of notes here and there, whether tucked into a pocket or slipped into a notebook.

content.text: Unofficial Work Logs (Not Suitable for Formal Submission)

Note 1

It's hard to say which is more miserable—the pea soup in the air or the pea pudding on my table.

I didn't finish today's report concerning the Fogwalker. He wasn't in his office, and I only happened upon him while wandering the streets at dinnertime. Trying to find someone in the fog is the worst game of hide-and-seek imaginable. The Fogwalker is piecing together a device he claims to be some sort of smog filtration machine ... I hope he doesn't truly believe he can handle all this fog on his own.

Note 2

Almost had my leg smashed in by a car. An Uluru leaflet dive-bombed my face, and with the Foundation uniform on, I couldn't get cross about it and tear the thing up.

HQ sent new tasks. Annoying. Frankly, under these circumstances, it feels inevitable that the London qualifiers will be canceled.

Note 3

Never thought I'd be drafting up paperwork to get the qualifiers canceled so soon. I'm oddly excited about the whole thing.

Note 4

Yes, it's all so strange. Everything here contradicts what we've managed to preserve in our records. But so what, why couldn't it have just been recording errors, bad recording practices, or outright falsified data that were passed on to us?

Meanwhile, I'm choking on coal dust that is falling as heavy as snow and putting up with a colleague who keeps getting lost in the fog. A stellar job experience.

Note 5

It's done, though there's a heap of follow-up work ahead. Honestly, I'm hoping that magnificent contraption will actually succeed. That way all these decorations won't go to waste, the tourists and athletes won't have wasted their time, and I won't have wasted all my pre-drafted paperwork.

Waste, waste, it was all a waste ... but I suppose things could have been so much worse.

items.text: One hour earlier.

items.speaker: Police Constable I
items.text: Please enter in an orderly manner, everyone. The ceremony will begin shortly.
Beside the device, the sign originally reading "London Air Pollution Auto-Detecting Purifier MK. II" now reads "MK. III" thanks to a single additional brushstroke.

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Freddy, can you see Mr. Fog? I can't see a thing past all these people.

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: You brought the telescope, didn't you, Dad? Maybe I can see if I look through it.

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Good idea. Here, take the telescope and get on my shoulders. Hold on tight, you hear? This crowd's rabid. All this pushin' and shovin' just to take a look at a machine!

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Then again, the most exciting thing we've had around here as of late is the rats fightin' in the underground.

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: I see him, Dad. I see Mr. Fog.

items.speaker: Will
items.text: What's he doin'?

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: Blimey! He's smackin' the machine! It's really strange lookin'.

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: About half the height of Mr. Fog, and connected to a very long tube and a massive funnel!

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: Ooh! What's that?!

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: Right there inside the machine, there's a huge mechanical organ or somethin', like a lung!

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Ah, sod it. Hold tight, Freddy. Dad's goin' to squeeze his way to the front!

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Alright, I can see them now. Eh? I don't recognize those two in uniform. Are they the officers sent from the Foundation headquarters in Australia?

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: That's what I heard. The Uluru Committee sent them here to supervise the qualifiers, and they'll report the results back to their headquarters, too.

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Ah, so it's down to them whether our athletes make it to the finals in Australia or not. I'm countin' on them.

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: Oh, please, Will. It's the players that you should count on, not the judges.

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Well, I hope they like Caroline as much as I do!

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: Look, Dad! Mr. Fog's about to give a demonstration of his purifier to the officers.

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: I heard that it can filter out the smog within ten yards of itself, and it only takes one night to process the waste. The qualifiers will only last two weeks, so it should manage splendidly.

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: It's workin'. It's workin'!

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Blimey, it's powerful! It's gulpin' down the smog faster than a builder downs a pint in the pub!

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: I wonder how it works. It's a miracle that a mechanical lung of this size can purify so much air without letting out any waste!

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: can purify so much air without letting out any waste!

items.speaker: Will
items.text: The smog's gettin' thinner. I can see more clearly now.

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: Look, it's even purifying the smog all the way out there! I dare say the ivy on my balcony will be enjoying fresh air within the hour!

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: Mr. Fog's smilin', Dad. Ain't that great?!

items.speaker: Will
items.text: It is. We ain't seen him smile for ages.

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: The hat looks happy too! It's dancin'!

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Is he doin' that Australian ranger dance again? Oh, look at the expression on those Foundation officers' faces.

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: Hmm. They don't look happy or mad. Is somethin' wrong?

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Woah! What's goin' on? The machine's shakin' like hell!
*beep-beep-beep*

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: What's that sound? Some kind of alarm?!
*beep-beep-beep*

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Oh! Christ! Cover your ears, Freddy! That howlin' will make you deaf. What in the bloody hell is goin' on?!
*boom*

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: D-Dad?

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Freddy? Are you alright?

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: I'm fine. It's the machine. It blew up!

items.speaker: Will
items.text: What?!

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: First the pipe blew open, then its glass belly shattered, and the mechanical lung rolled out from inside. It's vomitin' up black blood.

items.speaker: Will
items.text: There's no way.

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: And, and Mr. Fog!

items.speaker: Will
items.text: What happened to him?

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: He's coughin' and coughin'.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: Three and a half minutes.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member I
items.text: I guess neither one of us won that bet. It didn't even last half as long as I predicted.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: Don't be cruel, Gregory. We didn't come all this way just to laugh at these poor people.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member I
items.text: But they did do even worse than predicted. That's a fact, isn't it? And it proves that the London Climate Management Agency is nothing but a joke.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: Listen, Gregory. I know you must be exhausted from the long journey and your constant sneezing, but you can't say that to their faces. Let's just do our job and give them the news.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member I
items.text: What news?
She flips through the athlete roster in her hand.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: We have to tell them.
She verifies the list, ensuring that all the names of the arcanist athletes are accounted for.
When she's done, she lightly pats Mr. Fog on the shoulder.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: Mr. Fog? Mr. Fog?
Mr. Fog turns his head, his eyes vacant. It seems he hasn't yet got over the shock of this series of events.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: Please move aside. I need to use the microphone.
Mr. Fog slowly steps aside.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Oi, Miss. What are you ...
He quickly realizes the impropriety of his obstruction, tips his brim, and floats gently in the air.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: Ahem. Ladies and gentlemen, thank you all for coming to the ceremony today. We greatly appreciate your hospitality, and it heartens us to see you thriving despite the difficulties caused by the smog.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: However, it is clear to us that the London Air Pollution Auto-Detecting Purifier MK. III is not able to fulfill its duty.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: Barring an effective solution, the smog shrouding London will do irreversible damage to both the athletes and the general populace if they stay outdoors for too long.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: In light of this, and after much consideration, the Uluru International Committee has decided ...

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: To cancel the London Qualifiers for the Uluru Games.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: We will announce arrangements for the affected players once internal discussions are over.
Behind her cold mask, the woman methodically scans the crowd.
The previously raucous energy of the crowd has been replaced by a uniform disappointment.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: Thank you all for your hard work.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Are you sayin' that the London Qualifiers have been canceled?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: I'm afraid so.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: I wasn't there, but Mr. Brimley told me what happened in the stadium. Mr. Fog has locked himself in his office. He's refusing to speak to anyone.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: It seems there's nothing we can do about it.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Heh!
Willow pulls her hand away from Flutterpage's and gives her a solemn look.
Without a word, she turns and leaves.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Willow? Where you goin'?!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Willow! Ms. Willow!!
She tries to chase after her, but a flood of workers sent to take down the site blocks her way.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Willow!
Willow turns and gives her one last glance.
Before slipping away into the bustling crowd.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: *panting*
Flutterpage lifts her head, her eyes meeting Tooth Fairy's.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms.-Ms. Tooth Fairy ...

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Why?
